propositions.claim: EO 5614 of May 1, 1931 prescribes rules on reporting expenditures in the Budget under the Budget and Accounting Act, 1921.
propositions.quote: I hereby prescribe the following rules and regulations with regard to the reporting of expenditures in the Budget

propositions.claim: Para. 1 requires the Treasury Secretary to give the Budget Director a yearly expenditure statement on a checks-issued basis.
propositions.quote: the Secretary of the Treasury shall furnish the Director of the Bureau of the Budget with a detailed statement of the expenditures of the Government on the basis of checks issued

propositions.claim: Para. 2 requires each department and establishment head to report unexpended balances to the Treasury Secretary yearly.
propositions.quote: shall furnish the Secretary of the Treasury as soon as practicable after the close of each fiscal year with a detailed statement of the unexpended balances

propositions.claim: Para. 3 directs the Treasury Secretary to prescribe forms.
propositions.quote: The Secretary of the Treasury shall prescribe such forms as he may consider necessary to carry out the provisions of this order

propositions.claim: EO 8512 sec. 9 revokes EO 5614 by number and date.
propositions.quote: Executive Orders No. 5614 of May 1, 1931, No. 6226 of July 27, 1933, No. 6869 of October 10, 1934, No. 7126 of August 15, 1935, as amended
propositions.where: jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_8512.txt (5 FR 2849, sec. 9 on printed p. 2850; lines 265-268)

propositions.claim: The operative words of sec. 9 are a present revocation; EO 8512 is dated August 13, 1940.
propositions.quote: and all other orders or parts thereof inconsistent with the provisions of this order are hereby revoked.

propositions.claim: The National Archives (OFR) Executive Orders Disposition Tables page for 1940 records, in its entry for EO 8512 (signed August 13, 1940; 5 FR 2849, August 15, 1940), that EO 8512 revokes EO 5614. This is corroboration only; the ending rests on p5 and p6.
propositions.quote: Revokes: EO 5614, May 1, 1931; EO 6226, July 27, 1933; EO 6869, October 10, 1934; EO 7126, August 15, 1935
propositions.where: https://www.archives.gov/federal-register/executive-orders/1940.html (entry for Executive Order 8512; fetched 2026-11-18 through the fetch tool's page reader)

propositions.claim: The GPO slip-order printing carries the same text and closing number.
propositions.quote: THE WHITE HOUSE , May 1, 1931 . HERBERT HOOVER [No. 5614]

review.conclusion_reason: The accepted held printings establish all three operative paragraphs. EO 8512 section 9 expressly names the entire order and supplies the revocation language and August 13, 1940 date, satisfying the express_named_ending rule for every clause. T5 is withheld because p7's source attribution remains unverified.

verdicts.reason: The held OFR compilation identifies EO 5614, May 1, 1931, and reproduces the quoted prescription under the Budget and Accounting Act approved June 10, 1921.
Paragraph 1 contains the quotation and requires reporting after each fiscal year, including the stated fund classifications.
Paragraph 2 contains the quotation and applies to each executive department and independent establishment head; it covers balances held by disbursing officers and agents or to their official credit.
Paragraph 3 contains the quoted direction to prescribe necessary forms.

The held EO 8512 text and public Federal Register PDF, printed p. 2850, section 9, name EO 5614 and its date in the revocation sentence. The inconsistency qualification attaches to 'all other orders or parts thereof.'
Section 9 concludes 'are hereby revoked'; the signature block reads 'August 13, 1940' and '[No. 8512]'. Both the held text and public PDF confirm this.

The supplied slice reports both finding-aid entries, but is expressly a lead only. No complete API URL or location of the underlying 1989 table is supplied; their contents were not independently verified. The primary revocation text independently supports the substantive ending.
The cited held GPO OCR reproduces the same operative text and the quoted date, signature, and closing number; spacing differences are immaterial.
